top10.introHtml: These 10 picks rank condition first: verified clean titles, no-accident histories, and unusually low mileage float to the top — regardless of make. Price matters, but preservation matters more. Listings sourced from Cars.com, CarGurus, and AutoTrader as of November 11, 2026.

picks.notes: 46K original miles — rarest find in this entire search
picks.whyGood: A 1995 Jaguar XJS with only 46,000 miles is extraordinary — that's roughly 1,500 miles per year on a classic British grand tourer. The XJS 4+2 coupe offers true rear seat accommodations, buttery V12 ride, and timeless Pininfarina-inspired lines. AutoTrader confirms no accidents on the history report. At $8,499 for a car this preserved, you're buying a future collector piece at an everyday price.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax/AutoCheck report; cooling system (V12 runs hot if neglected); timing chain/tensioners; hydraulic system for the top; all electrics functional (windows, locks, top); find an independent Jaguar specialist for a pre-purchase inspection.
picks.bottomLine: If 46,000 documented miles on a V12 Jaguar XJS checks out, this is the most remarkable find in this month's results — buy it.

picks.notes: 34K miles in 19 years — an absurdly well-preserved E92-era cabrio
picks.whyGood: Only 34,431 miles on a 2007 BMW 328i Convertible with clean title and no accidents — that averages under 1,900 miles per year. The E93 328i features a silky 3.0L inline-six, proper four-seat convertible top, and bulletproof reliability when well maintained. This level of preservation at $14,485 is exceptional value for a modern classic that will only appreciate.
picks.whatToVerify: Full history report; check rubber seals and convertible top mechanism for dry rot (low miles but age); coolant expansion tank; valve cover gaskets; ask why mileage is so low (storage? second car?); have BMW specialist inspect.
picks.bottomLine: 34K miles and clean title on a 2007 BMW convertible is a unicorn find — worth the premium price at the top of your budget.

picks.notes: E46 330Ci — 64K miles on the definitive driver's convertible
picks.whyGood: The E46 BMW 330Ci Convertible is widely regarded as the best driver's convertible ever built at this price point. With only 64,358 miles, the M54 3.0L straight-six has barely been broken in. Clean title, no accidents, four proper seats, and sharp 2000s styling that still turns heads. The E46 is reliable, parts are plentiful, and community support is massive.
picks.whatToVerify: Cooling system (E46 plastic components degrade by age, not miles — replace proactively); convertible top condition and hydraulics; oil for cooling system contamination; thrust arm bushings; CCC/iDrive if equipped.
picks.bottomLine: An E46 330Ci with 64K miles and clean history at $9,495 is the kind of car enthusiasts wait years to find.

picks.notes: N54 twin-turbo 300hp at 48K miles — exceptional mileage for this engine
picks.whyGood: The BMW 135i packs a N54 twin-turbocharged 3.0L inline-six producing 300hp in a compact, nimble convertible body. At only 48,000 miles, the N54 is barely into its prime — these engines commonly run 150K+ miles with proper maintenance. The 1 Series Convertible has four seats, a fully automatic power top, and handles like a true sports car. This is $11,595 well spent.
picks.whatToVerify: N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) history — common recall item, verify replaced; wastegate rattle; charge pipe condition; full Carfax; ask for maintenance records particularly for HPFP and turbos.
picks.bottomLine: A sub-50K mile N54 twin-turbo BMW convertible at $11,595 is a legitimately great deal for enthusiasts who want real performance.

picks.notes: V8 CLK 500 Cabriolet — clean title + no accidents under $8K
picks.whyGood: The CLK 500 Cabriolet features Mercedes' naturally aspirated 5.0L V8 producing 302hp — in a full four-seat, fully-lined convertible with that signature Benz luxury feel. At $7,900 with clean title and no accident history on only 82,000 miles, this is tremendous value for a genuine V8 Mercedes. The W209 CLK is a timeless design with four proper adult seats.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; air suspension (if equipped); SBC brake system recall/replacement (critical safety item on W211/W209 era); transmission service history; climate control blend doors; check all electrics and convertible roof.
picks.bottomLine: V8 Mercedes Cabriolet with clean history under $8K — this is what the budget convertible hunt is for.

picks.notes: Quattro AWD A5 Cabriolet — clean history at 80K miles for $8,495
picks.whyGood: The Audi A5 Cabriolet is one of the most beautiful convertibles ever designed — and the Quattro all-wheel-drive makes it genuinely usable year-round in the mid-Atlantic. At 80,410 miles with clean title and no accidents, this 2012 is well into its sweet spot. The 2.0T TFSI makes 211hp, pairs beautifully with the slick 8-speed, and the interior quality is notably above BMW and Mercedes at this price range.
picks.whatToVerify: Timing chain (early 2.0T engines had chain issues; verify TSB or replacement); DSG/S-tronic service history; Carfax full report; test all MMI functions; convertible top operation.
picks.bottomLine: Quattro all-wheel-drive in a stunning A5 convertible with clean history for $8,495 — this checks every box.

picks.notes: Power-folding hardtop + 332hp V6 + Great Price badge — premium convertible under $13K
picks.whyGood: The G37 Convertible is INFINITI's best-ever product: a power-folding metal hardtop (not a cloth top — a full steel retractable roof) over four proper seats, powered by the legendary 3.7L VQ37 V6 producing 332hp. This is a car that competes with far more expensive European convertibles. AutoTrader shows Great Price badge and no accidents on the history report.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; hardtop mechanism operation (run the top through several full open/close cycles); CVT or 7AT service history; timing chain (Nissan/Infiniti VQ engines have known chain stretch on neglected examples); brake condition.
picks.bottomLine: A metal hardtop convertible with 332hp and no accidents at $12,088 is exceptional value — this is a Grand Touring car at a commuter car price.

picks.notes: Supercharged 3.0T Quattro V6 — the S5 Cabriolet is the rarest Audi in this pool
picks.whyGood: The S5 Cabriolet is a rarer and more desirable machine than the standard A5: 333hp supercharged 3.0 TFSI V6 with Quattro AWD, sport-tuned suspension, and S-line aesthetics. At $10,489 and 92K miles this is a genuine bargain for a car that retailed over $60,000 new. Quattro AWD means it's as useful in November as July.
picks.whatToVerify: Supercharger belt service history; timing chain; Quattro Haldex/Torsen diff fluid; DSG/S-tronic service; check for any front end accident damage on CarFax; all S-line suspension components for wear.
picks.bottomLine: A supercharged V6 Quattro S5 Cabriolet for $10,489 is a legitimately special find — just budget for thorough maintenance.

picks.notes: CarGurus 'Great Deal' at $7,888 — most affordable BMW 3 Series in results
picks.whyGood: CarGurus flags this 2011 BMW 328i Convertible as a Great Deal at $7,888 — that is a legitimately good price for an E93 cabrio with sub-90K miles. The N52 3.0L inline-six is smooth, reliable, and characterful. Four genuine seats, proper folding fabric top, and BMW's precise handling make this the best entry point into the BMW convertible ownership experience at this budget.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; cooling system components (all plastic parts age-related regardless of mileage on N52); valve cover gasket; oil for leaks; test convertible roof through full cycle; check brake thickness.
picks.bottomLine: A sub-$8K Great Deal on an E93 BMW 328i Convertible with under 90K miles is excellent value — verify history and have a BMW shop check it over.

picks.notes: 2018 model year — the most modern car in this entire search pool
picks.whyGood: The 2018 BMW 430i xDrive Convertible is 7 years newer than the next-oldest BMW in these results — it brings Apple CarPlay, the iDrive 6 infotainment system, 252hp TwinPower turbo, and xDrive all-wheel-drive. At $14,999 with clean title and no accidents, you get a genuinely modern luxury convertible. The 430i Convertible is the most feature-rich, warranty-service-friendly choice in this search.
picks.whatToVerify: Carfax full report (verify no accidents); verify xDrive AWD operational (front driveshaft, Haldex unit); timing chain (B46/B48 engines have better reliability than N54 but verify no oil consumption); check iDrive for all OEM features.
picks.bottomLine: If modern tech and warranty peace-of-mind matter, the 2018 430i is the buy — it's the only car in results young enough to still find dealer support.

manual10.introHtml: Stick-shift convertibles are rare in this price range — most automatics dominate the used market. These picks are likely candidates for manual transmission based on model and trim, but always call ahead to confirm before making the drive. A confirmed 6-speed manual on any of these would be a great find.

picks.notes: E46 330Ci — available with classic 5-speed Getrag manual; verify at viewing
picks.whyGood: The E46 BMW 330Ci was available with either a 5-speed Getrag manual or a 5-speed ZF automatic. At 64K miles with clean history, if this one has the manual it is an extraordinary find — the M54+Getrag combination is considered the last truly analog BMW driving experience. Even if automatic, it's the best-value E46 cabrio in this search.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm transmission is manual before making appointment; clutch wear; cooling system age-related items (hoses, expansion tank, thermostat); E46 subframe inspection.
picks.bottomLine: Call ahead to verify manual — if confirmed, this 64K-mile E46 goes straight to the top of the whole list.

picks.notes: BMW 128i Convertible — routinely specified with 6-speed manual; highest miles in pool
picks.whyGood: The BMW 128i was specifically marketed as the driver's-focused 1 Series, and a significant percentage were ordered with the 6-speed manual. The N52 3.0L straight-six pairs beautifully with the short-throw gearbox. High mileage (147K) is reflected in the $7,485 price — the lowest BMW price in the entire search. If manual, this is a cheap way into proper BMW engagement.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm manual before visiting; at 147K miles: clutch condition, cooling system, valve cover gasket; full Carfax despite clean title claim; oil leaks.
picks.bottomLine: Cheap entry for stick-shift BMW buyers — verify manual transmission and inspect thoroughly given the mileage.

picks.notes: 335i Convertible — twin-turbo available with 6-speed manual; best performance value
picks.whyGood: The 2009 BMW 335i Convertible with the N54 twin-turbo and 6-speed manual is the unicorn pick of this search if confirmed manual. 300hp through a row-your-own gearbox in an open-top car at $8,000 — this is the stuff of enthusiast dreams. Even at 107K miles, the N54 is known for longevity with proper maintenance.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm manual transmission; N54 HPFP recall status; wastegate rattle; charge pipe condition; full Carfax; cooling system; timing chain.
picks.bottomLine: If this 335i has a 6-speed, it may be the most engaging driver's car in the entire search at any price.

picks.notes: 1995 Firebird convertible — clean title + no accidents; likely T56 6-speed or 4L60E auto
picks.whyGood: The 1995 Pontiac Firebird Convertible is a true American classic — available with either the T56 6-speed manual or 4L60E automatic behind the 3800 V6 or LT1 V8. At $7,500 with clean title and no accidents, this is an affordable piece of GM F-body history. The 4-seat convertible body is rarer than the coupe and increasingly collectible.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm engine (V6 3800 or V8 LT1) and transmission type; rust inspection (floors, frame rails); convertible top seal condition; LT1 optispark distributor if V8 (known weak point).
picks.bottomLine: A clean-title F-body convertible under $8K — if the V8 LT1 is confirmed and T56 manual, this is a true bargain classic.

picks.notes: 2012 BMW 128i — cleaner, lower-mile option vs the 2011; likely 6-speed manual available
picks.whyGood: The 2012 BMW 128i Convertible at 86,671 miles represents a cleaner, later model of the same enthusiast-favorite 1 Series. At $12,704 it's pricier than the 2011, but the lower mileage and clean title justify the difference. If spec'd with 6-speed manual, this is a sport BMW convertible that provides real driving engagement at a fraction of new-car cost.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm manual or automatic before visiting; cooling system; full Carfax; clutch wear if manual.
picks.bottomLine: Better condition and lower miles than the 2011 — worth the premium if the manual box is confirmed.

mustangs.introHtml: All 2005 and newer Ford Mustang Convertibles found in this search, sorted by price. Every listing here is a V6 model — the most affordable and practical Mustang convertible for daily use. The S197 platform (2005–2014) is proven, parts are plentiful, and the community is massive. Avoid pre-2005 Mustangs in this budget — the SN95 chassis is showing its age.

picks.notes: Cheapest Mustang in results — 167K miles reflected in price
picks.whyGood: At $8,048 this is the most affordable 2014 Mustang V6 Convertible in the search. The 3.7L V6 is surprisingly spirited at 305hp, and the S197 Mustang Convertible has genuine rear seats. High mileage (167.5K) is the tradeoff but the V6 automatic drivetrain is known for longevity.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; cooling system; transmission fluid condition; convertible top seal; exhaust for signs of overheating history.
picks.bottomLine: High miles but the cheapest entry into 2014 Mustang convertible ownership — accept the mileage or step up to one of the lower-mile options below.

picks.notes: No accidents reported — solid mid-price Mustang at 121K miles
picks.whyGood: AutoTrader confirms no accident history on this 2014 Mustang V6 Convertible. At 121,000 miles and $10,390 this hits the sweet spot between affordability and reasonable mileage for the S197 chassis. The V6 is a known quantity: low maintenance cost, abundant parts, easy to service.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; check for any undercarriage rust; brake condition; convertible top fabric and seals.
picks.bottomLine: No-accident 2014 Mustang convertible at a reasonable price — good all-around value.

picks.notes: Clean title + no accidents — slightly higher mileage, fully documented
picks.whyGood: Cars.com shows clean title and no accident history on this 2014 Mustang V6 Convertible. At $10,478 and 128K miles it costs slightly more per mile than #2 above, but the documented clean title adds confidence. Standard S197 Mustang virtues apply.
picks.whatToVerify: Cross-reference Carfax with Cars.com data; inspect convertible top; brake and tire condition.
picks.bottomLine: Fully documented clean history — worth the slight price premium over similar-mileage examples.

picks.notes: Best mileage among the 2014 Mustangs — 109K with clean history
picks.whyGood: Among the 2014 Mustang convertibles in this search, this one has the lowest mileage (109,452) with clean title and no accidents. At $10,495 the per-mile value is the best in the group. The S197 platform at this mileage is well-proven and has abundant support from the Mustang community.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; look for convertible top condition specifically; check for any signs of water intrusion; brake thickness.
picks.bottomLine: Best mileage among 2014 Mustang convertibles with clean history — the top Mustang pick in this search.

picks.notes: V6 Premium trim — sub-100K miles on a 2013 Mustang convertible
picks.whyGood: The only 2013 Mustang convertible in results, and the V6 Premium trim adds upgraded audio, heated seats, and aluminum interior accents over base. At 97,202 miles this is the only 2005+ Mustang convertible in this search under 100K miles — a meaningful threshold for buyers focused on longevity. Clean title and no accidents.
picks.whatToVerify: Full Carfax; cooling system; verify Premium features all operational (heated seats, Shaker audio if equipped); convertible top condition.
picks.bottomLine: Only sub-100K Mustang convertible in results with clean history — if you want the freshest 'Stang, this is the one.
